title: SRE / Platform Qualifier Pocket (draft)
content:
Purpose:
Quick, portable reference for sellers and SEs to rapidly qualify platform/SRE stakeholders during discovery and pilot planning. Aim: identify whether Redwood's routing/caching/fallback controls solve the customer's operational constraints and reduce risk for a pilot.

Audience:
- Platform engineers, SRE leads, cloud infra architects at prospects
- Sales engineers prepping for a 30–45m technical discovery or pilot scoping call

TL;DR elevator (30s):
We provide a unified inference runtime that isolates noisy tenants, routes traffic by latency/cost policy, and fails over predictably so your customer-facing models hit SLOs without wasting GPU spend. For pilots we scope a small path (1–2 endpoints), enforce circuit-breaker SLOs, and instrument token-level cost dashboards so you can rollback or scale on measurable signals.

90s technical opener (for SE):
"Tell me about your 95th percentile latency goal for production traffic, and any requests that can tolerate increased latency for cost savings. We usually map those to two routes: a low-latency route (dedicated or hosted with pre-warmed capacity) and a cost-first route (quantized / relaxed model), then set transparent fallbacks if the primary route breaches capacity."

Quick qualifier checklist (ask these in first 10m):
- Production SLA target (p95/p99) and transaction types that are latency-sensitive?
- Burst pattern: steady QPS vs spiky (hourly/dayly spikes)? Peak QPS number and average token length?
- Data residency / network constraints (VPC, private infra, on-prem)?
- Security / compliance gates (SOC2, PCI, HIPAA) or required certs?
- Incident playbooks: who owns customer-visible degradation? Slack channels + runbooks?
- Model consistency expectations: can output quality vary across fallbacks? Acceptable delta?
- Cost ownership: does infra cost sit with product, platform, or centralized Cloud FinOps?

SLO mapping shorthand (how to map customer asks into Redwood controls):
- p95 <= 200ms (interactive UI) -> Dedicated pool with autoscaling headroom + warm KV cache prefill; strict routing policy to avoid multi-tenant contention.
- p95 200–800ms (async UX / batch-like) -> Shared hosted route + batch size tuning + 8-bit quantized model variant.
- p99 requirements -> set p99 SLO but add automatic fallback to cheaper compatible variant when latency risk detected.

Decision heuristics for routing & fallback (one-liners sellers can use):
- If UX is interactive and p95 < 300ms required -> recommend dedicated with burst reservation.
- If traffic is unpredictable but cost matters -> start hosted with autoscaling cap + progressive canary.
- If regulated data -> push for Private (VPC) pilot with limited endpoints and strict logging.

Pilot scoping checklist (deliverables for a 4-week trial):
- 1–2 prioritized routes (route = endpoint + model + prompt template)
- Baseline perf run (48–72h) to capture latency, token distribution, and cache-hit rates
- Acceptance metrics: p95 latency, cost per 1k tokens, error rate, quality delta vs control prompts
- Rollout policy: canary 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 3 days with auto rollback threshold (p95 increase > 2x or error spike > 0.5%)
- Observability handoff: access to Redwood Console subset and dashboard link + example tracing spans

Recommended pilot signals & thresholds (starter):
- Latency p95 baseline + 1.5x -> trigger scale-up/alert
- Token cost per route above expected budget by 20% -> trigger sample review + model/quantization recommendation
- Cache hit rate < 10% for prefix-heavy workloads -> enable prefix caching config

Fallback policy examples (copy-paste into routing config conversation):
- primary: model-A-standard (low-latency)
- fallback-1: model-A-quantized (higher latency tolerance, lower cost)
- fallback-2: model-B-small (reduced hallucination risk for short answers)
Notes: If primary latency > threshold OR queue_length > N, route to fallback-1. If fallback quality score < Q or token cost threshold crossed, fail open to small model with human-in-loop flag.

Script snippets for SE during call (quick prompts):
- "If we see sustained p95 increases, would you want automatic fallback or a pager alert first?"
- "Who owns the cost delta during a pilot—platform team or product? We can set a soft budget cap to avoid surprises."
- "Which three prompts are most critical for customer experience? We'll baseline those for quality regressions."

Common objections + tight responses (for sellers):
- "We can’t risk inconsistent answers across models." -> "We'll baseline the canonical prompts and set quality regression thresholds; fallback only triggers on operational failure and is logged for auditing. You can set human review for any flagged responses."
- "We already host models internally." -> "We can interop: Redwood can route to your private endpoint for critical paths while offering hosting for burst/offload—single API surface for both."
- "Costs are unpredictable." -> "Pilot includes token-level dashboards and soft caps; Redwood Optimize provides batching/quantization suggestions to reduce unit cost after baseline."

Operational playbook snippet (post-pilot handoff):
- 7-day follow-up: review SLOs and incidents, gather 3–5 representative failures
- 30-day ramp: tighten canary windows and decrease threshold tolerances as confidence grows
- Optional: migrate critical routes to Dedicated with reserved capacity and scheduled pre-warms

Open questions / TODOs (internal notes):
- Need example dashboard screenshot that highlights token-cost by route (ask Observability team for a 2-up mock). 
- Validate wording around "fail open to small model" with Legal for regulated verticals.
- Confirm sample thresholds and names with Product (routing config API v2).

Slack templates (copyable):
- Incident alert -> "[Redwood Pilot] Route <route-name> p95 > <threshold> for 15m. Auto-fallback engaged. Pager: @sre-oncall"
- Pilot kick -> "Kicking off Redwood pilot for <org>. Primary route = <route>, fallback = <variant>. Dashboard: <link>. Owner: <engineer>"

Appendix: quick links for SE/AE
- Routing policy examples repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing-policy-examples
- Console access request form: https://internal.redwood.ai/console-access
- Playbook reference: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/SRE+playbook+index

Notes to self: keep this pocket under 1 page for slide deck insert. Need customer-facing language for legal/regulated that swaps "fail open" -> "degrade to low-risk path with audit logs" for final version.

End.
